feedback: If a learner answers that replanting instantly cancels the release, note that regrowth takes decades to re-store carbon that burning released in a short time.
If a learner only mentions temperature, remind them transpiration recycles water that feeds rain, so losing forest can reduce rainfall regionally and beyond.
Tie the 'lungs' myth probe here: redirect from oxygen to carbon storage and rainfall as the real climate roles.
activities.intendedInsight: Learners can state the sink idea, the carbon-release-on-burning mechanism, the deforestation→CO2→warming chain, and transfer the two-way idea to new cases (regrowth takes decades; less transpiration can reduce rainfall in regions far off).
learnerActions: Complete the statement: an intact rainforest acts as a carbon ____ (sink).
State what is released into the atmosphere when a forest is burned, and where that carbon had been stored.
Put the steps in order: forest cleared/burned → stored carbon released as CO2 → more CO2 in the atmosphere → global temperatures rise.
Answer: if a country replants a forest, does that instantly cancel the carbon released when the old one burned? Explain why or why not.
Answer: how could losing a rainforest change rainfall far away, not just the local temperature?
activities.title: Explain and sequence the deforestation chain

feedback: If a learner gives the oxygen/lungs reason as the main role, explain that respiration and decay consume oxygen too, so net output is small, and redirect to carbon storage and rainfall.
Confirm when a learner rejects the slogan AND names carbon storage, rainfall, and the sink→source flip rather than listing them as unconnected facts.
activities.intendedInsight: The 'lungs/oxygen' slogan is misleading because a mature forest's NET oxygen output is small; the real climate importance is carbon storage and rainfall, and the same forest becomes a carbon source when burned.
learnerActions: Respond to the claim: 'Rainforests matter for climate mainly because they make most of the oxygen we breathe.' Decide whether this is the main reason, and explain why.
Explain what else in a mature forest uses up oxygen (plants and soil organisms respire; decay consumes oxygen too), so its net oxygen output is small.
State the two real climate roles: carbon storage (a sink) and transpiration-driven rainfall.
Consider that scientists think much of Earth's oxygen comes from ocean phytoplankton, not from rainforests — another reason the 'lungs' slogan is misleading.
activities.title: Bust the 'lungs of the planet' myth
